title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
title_zh: Cogentic：面向自动证明发现的多智能体编排

paragraphs.en: We present Cogentic, a multi-agent harness for automated proof discovery on open research problems. While frontier language models can generate strong mathematical ideas in a single shot, single-shot generation is often insufficient for open problems that require exploring multiple competing conjectures, overcoming subtle technical obstructions, and retaining intermediate progress over a long horizon. Cogentic addresses these challenges through an iterative prove–verify loop in which an orchestrator allocates a population of independent provers across distinct proof directions, subjects their output to adversarial verification by several specialized components, and promotes confirmed intermediate results into a persistent verified ledger that later rounds build on. The harness is designed to be able to solve research-level math and theoretical computer science problems. Using either Gemini 3.1 Pro or an early version of Gemini 4 Argon as the base model, Cogentic produced novel results on open problems across online learning, auction theory, and mechanism design. Each result was independently verified by domain experts and is developed in full in companion papers. We list these results, and new ones as they are verified, at https://sites.google.com/view/cogentic .

paragraphs.en: We introduce Cogentic, a multi-agent harness for proof discovery on open research problems. Inspired by our own experience conducting research in theoretical computer science and mathematics, the harness divides the work like a research group would: an orchestrator decides what gets worked on, provers draft proofs in parallel, and verifiers read those drafts looking for potential issues. We found that our system is quite efficient: The results reported here were based on Cogentic runs (each powered entirely by either Gemini 3.1 Pro or an early version of Gemini 4 Argon) which used O ⁡ ( 100 ) O(100) model calls for most problems, and O ⁡ ( 1000 ) O(1000) for the hardest. The system has headroom for further optimization of the number of calls but also allows for naturally scaling up to solve harder problems. A key feature of the system is that it only needs a problem statement, without any expert hints, and can work autonomously until it produces a result in the form of a paper. To evaluate the harness, we focus on problem domains within our own areas of expertise, targeting natural-language, human-readable proofs where we can directly verify the mathematical reasoning and provide exposition surrounding the background of the paper and the novel techniques that the system generates.
paragraphs.zh: 我们推出了 Cogentic，一个用于在开放研究问题中发现证明的多智能体框架。 受我们在理论计算机科学和数学领域开展研究的亲身经历启发，该框架将工作分配方式模拟了一个研究团队：协调器决定处理哪些任务，证明生成器并行起草证明，而验证器则阅读这些草稿以发现潜在问题。 我们发现该系统效率相当高：本文报告的结果基于 Cogentic 的运行（每次运行完全由 Gemini 3.1 Pro 或 Gemini 4 Argon 早期版本提供支持），在大多数问题上仅需 O(100) 次模型调用，而在最困难的问题上则需要 O(1000) 次。 该系统在进一步优化调用次数方面仍有空间，同时也能自然扩展以解决更复杂的问题。 该系统的一个关键特性是，它只需要问题陈述，无需任何专家提示，并且能够自主运行，直到以论文形式产出结果。 为了评估该框架，我们专注于自身专业领域内的研究问题，目标是生成人类可读的自然语言证明，这样我们就能直接验证其中的数学推理，并对论文的背景以及系统生成的创新方法进行阐述。

paragraphs.en: Interactive theorem provers — Lean ( Moura and Ullrich, 2021 ) , Isabelle/HOL ( Nipkow et al., 2002 ) , Coq ( Castéran and Bertot, 2004 ) — provide machine-checked guarantees, and a substantial line of work uses language models to lower the cost of obtaining them: retrieving premises and generating tactics ( Yang et al., 2023 ) , drafting an informal proof and compiling it into a formal sketch ( Jiang et al., 2022 ) , and training for olympiad-level formal reasoning with reinforcement learning ( Hubert et al., 2026 ) . More recently the same machinery has been used on open research problems ( Tsoukalas et al., 2026 ) . In contrast, Cogentic operates in natural language, producing mathematical prose that domain experts can verify.
paragraphs.zh: 交互式定理证明器——Lean（Moura 和 Ullrich，2021）、Isabelle/HOL（Nipkow 等，2002）以及 Coq（Castéran 和 Bertot，2004）——能够提供机器验证的保证，而大量研究则利用语言模型来降低获取这些保证的成本：例如检索前提并生成策略（Yang 等，2023）、起草非正式证明并将其编译为正式草图（Jiang 等，2022），以及通过强化学习训练智能体进行奥林匹克竞赛级别的正式推理（Hubert 等，2026）。 近期，同样的技术也被应用于开放的研究问题（Tsoukalas 等，2026）。 相比之下，Cogentic 以自然语言运行，能够生成领域专家可以验证的数学文本。

paragraphs.en: A distinct and highly successful line of work uses language models to search for mathematical objects rather than for arguments. Program search has discovered new constructions in extremal combinatorics ( Romera-Paredes et al., 2024 ) , evolutionary coding agents have improved algorithms and bounds ( Novikov et al., 2025 ) , and related systems perform test-time learning on open problems ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Yuksekgonul et al., 2026 ) or explore many problems at once ( Georgiev et al., 2025 ) . Neuro-symbolic search attains medal-level performance in olympiad geometry by pairing a learned proposer with a symbolic engine ( Trinh et al., 2024 ) . The same recipe extends beyond mathematics to writing expert-level empirical research software under a quality metric ( Aygün et al., 2026 ) . What each of these approaches requires is a cheap, faithful, and machine-computable score. Sometimes theorems can be proven by reducing the question to finding mathematical structures with certain properties: e.g., Nagda et al. (2026) found proofs of inapproximability for combinatorial problems by finding extremal structures, and ( Cai et al., 2026f ) found bounds on gain from bilateral trade by finding extremal probability distributions, both using AlphaEvolve ( Novikov et al., 2025 ) with such oracles. However, not every problem is amenable to such an approach.
paragraphs.zh: 一种独特且非常成功的工作路线是利用语言模型来搜索数学对象，而非搜索论证。 程序搜索已在极值组合学领域发现了新的构造（Romera-Paredes 等人，2024），进化编码智能体改进了算法和界限（Novikov 等人，2025），而相关系统则对开放问题执行测试时学习（Wang 等人，2025；Yuksekgonul 等人，2026）或同时探索多个问题（Georgiev 等人，2025）。 神经符号搜索通过将已学习的命题生成器与符号引擎相结合，在奥林匹克几何学竞赛中达到了奖牌级表现（Trinh 等人，2024）。 同样的方法还可扩展至数学之外的领域，例如根据质量指标编写专家级的实证研究软件（Aygün 等人，2026）。 这些方法各自都需要一个廉价、可靠且可机器计算的评分标准。 有时，定理可以通过将问题归约为寻找具有特定属性的数学结构来证明：例如，Nagda 等人 （2026）通过寻找极值结构，为组合问题找到了不可近似性的证明；而（Cai 等人，2026f）则通过寻找极值概率分布，得出了双边贸易收益的界限。两者均使用了配备此类神谕的 AlphaEvolve（Novikov 等人，2025）。 然而，并非所有问题都适合采用这种方法。

paragraphs.en: A second line of work is based on scaling the LLM inference budget, perhaps through multiple model calls, to solve more complex tasks. The base case is simply to sample more — chain-of-thought prompting ( Wei et al., 2022 ) , self-consistency across sampled solutions ( Wang et al., 2022 ) , and repeated sampling with a selector over the candidates ( Brown et al., 2024 ; Snell et al., 2024 ) . Another approach is to scale the inference via multi-agent interaction. Debate between instances has been reported to improve factuality and reasoning ( Du et al., 2024 ; Liang et al., 2024 ) , and models have been used to evaluate the work of other models ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ) . Our framework builds on an iterative interaction between provers and verifiers. The verifiers are adversarial and begin with the assumption that the proofs are incorrect or incomplete. We explain our framework in more detail in Section 2 .
paragraphs.zh: 第二类工作基于扩大 LLM 推理预算，或许通过多次模型调用，来解决更复杂的任务。 基础方法就是简单地增加采样次数——思维链提示（Wei et al., 2022）、在采样解中实现自一致性（Wang et al., 2022），以及使用选择器对候选解进行重复采样（Brown et al., 2024；Snell et al., 2024）。 另一种方法是通过多智能体交互来扩大推理能力。 已有研究指出，实例之间的辩论能够提升事实性和推理能力（Du et al., 2024；Liang et al., 2024），并且模型也被用于评估其他模型的工作成果（Zhuge et al., 2024）。 我们的框架建立在证明者与验证者之间的迭代交互之上。 验证者之间是相互对抗的，并且最初假设证明是错误的或不完整的。 我们将在第 2 节中更详细地解释我们的框架。

paragraphs.en: Finally, we place our contributions against recent milestones obtained with large agentic systems, including the resolution of a Millennium Prize problem ( OpenAI, 2026b ) and other long-standing mathematical conjectures ( OpenAI, 2026a ; Anthropic, 2026 ) . We focus on problems in our areas of expertise, at the hardness level of open questions in flagship theoretical computer science conferences like STOC and FOCS, using a relatively low inference budget, O ⁡ ( 100 ) O(100) to O ⁡ ( 1000 ) O(1000) Gemini calls per problem.

paragraphs.en: Cogentic consists of a group of agents working on a single problem. They share a workspace on disk and are coordinated by an orchestrator that decides which of them runs, when, and on what.
paragraphs.zh: Cogentic 由一组共同解决单一问题的智能体组成。 它们在磁盘上共享一个工作区，并由一个协调器进行协调，该协调器决定哪些智能体在何时运行以及运行什么内容。

paragraphs.en: We outline the main components of our system below.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在下文概述了系统的主要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: The orchestrator serves as the central controller: it tracks global state, partitions prover slots across research directions, spawns summarizers to condense history into targeted briefings for individual provers, evaluates verifier consensus, and manages ledgers that store important findings obtained so far and records that track prior proof attempts and their verdicts. The orchestrator does not perform mathematical derivations itself.
paragraphs.zh: 协调器充当中央控制器：它跟踪全局状态，将证明者分配槽位划分到不同的研究方向，启动摘要生成器以将历史信息浓缩为针对各个证明者的定向简报，评估验证器的一致性，并管理账本——这些账本存储迄今获得的重要发现，以及记录先前证明尝试及其结果的日志。 协调器本身并不执行数学推导。

paragraphs.en: Literature reviewers search for related work and retrieve information such as definitions and theorems that a prover is likely to need. They can also be sent out again mid-run to do a more targeted search and find results that can help overcome ongoing technical barriers.
paragraphs.zh: 文献评审员会搜索相关研究，并检索证明者可能需要使用的定义和定理等信息。 在运行过程中，也可以再次派它们执行更精准地搜索，以找到有助于克服当前技术障碍的结果。

paragraphs.en: Provers generate candidate proofs independently and in parallel based on assigned briefings that selectively summarize findings obtained so far.
paragraphs.zh: 证明生成器基于分配给它们的简报独立且并行地生成候选证明，这些简报会选择性总结迄今获得的发现。

paragraphs.en: Verifiers critique candidate solutions from complementary angles and scopes.
paragraphs.zh: 验证器从互补的角度和范围对候选解决方案进行批判性评估。

paragraphs.en: The record keeps track of prover attempts and their corresponding critiques from verifiers, and the ledger keeps track of verified intermediate lemmas that came out of proof attempts. These are the central ways that our agents communicate and document progress, as explained in more detail below.
paragraphs.zh: 该记录会追踪证明者的尝试以及验证者对此提出的相应批评，而账本则会记录在证明尝试中产生的已验证的中间引理。 正如下文将更详细地解释的那样，这些是我们智能体之间进行沟通和记录进展的主要方式。

paragraphs.en: An advisor reads outputs across rounds to help the orchestrator decide how to control and allocate prover attempts and what to adjust the instructions given to each individual prover for the next round.

paragraphs.en: Finally, a consolidation stage formats and audits the final manuscript.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，整合阶段会对最终手稿进行格式整理和审核。

paragraphs.en: The work proceeds in rounds (Figure 1 ). A round produces a batch of candidate proofs, puts them through verification, and writes into the record and the verified ledger that the next round starts from. Rounds continue until a draft clears verification or until the budget runs out.
paragraphs.zh: 该工作按轮次进行（图 1）。 每一轮都会生成一批候选证明，对其进行验证，并在记录表和已验证账本中写入下一轮开始的位置。 轮次将持续进行，直到某份草案通过验证，或者预算用尽为止。

paragraphs.en: A round opens with the orchestrator planning the work: how many provers to run, and what direction each should attend to. A direction here is a specific claim (e.g., a bound, a constant, a construction), finding counterexamples, or as the run goes on, repairing and finalizing promising proofs. A prover is assigned to a direction to work on, but not how to work on it. It reads what has been attempted previously for that direction, what the verifiers said about those attempts, as well as common information like the literature survey and the verified ledger, and chooses its own next step.
paragraphs.zh: 一轮开始于协调者规划工作：需要运行多少个证明者，以及每个证明者应关注哪个方向。 此处的“方向”指一个具体的主张（例如，一个界限、一个常数、一个构造），寻找反例，或者随着运行过程推进，修正并完善有希望的证明。 一个证明者会被分配到一个方向上开展工作，但不会被告知具体如何开展。 它会读取此前针对该方向已尝试过的方法、验证器对这些尝试的反馈，以及文献综述和已验证账本等通用信息，然后选择自己的下一步行动。

paragraphs.en: As the run goes on, the material relevant to a prover grows in volume. Rather than passing all of it as input, each prover sees only a briefing, written for it by a summarizer, which is spawned by the orchestrator. The summarizer reads all prior attempts and their verdicts, selects the most informative ones as context, and gives suggestions for possible next steps, based on what has worked and what has not. Each summarizer produces its briefing independently, so provers in the same round receive different readings of the same history. Longer documents are given as paths rather than quoted in full, so a prover (which itself is an agent, such as an Antigravity agent ( The Antigravity Team, 2025 ) ) can open what it wants to read selectively.
paragraphs.zh: 随着运行过程的推进，与证明者相关的材料体量会不断增加。 而非将所有材料作为输入传递，每个证明者只会看到一份简报——这份简报由协调器生成的摘要器专门为其编写。 摘要器会读取所有先前的尝试及其判定结果，从中挑选信息量最大的内容作为上下文，并基于哪些方法有效、哪些无效，提出可能的后续步骤建议。 每个摘要器都独立生成自己的简报，因此同一轮中的证明者会获得对相同历史记录的不同解读。 较长的文档以路径形式提供，而非完整引用，这样证明者（其本身也是一个智能体，例如反重力智能体（The Antigravity Team, 2025））就可以选择性打开自己希望阅读的内容。

paragraphs.en: After each prover completes a proof, it is read by a verifier whose task is to check the correctness of the proof. A separate verifier reads all of the round’s drafts side by side, which allows it to spot shared blind spots and compare the strengths of individual proofs. A draft is accepted only when it passes both verifiers. Both are adversarial: they start from the assumption that every step is wrong until justified, and that every citation is incorrect until checked.
paragraphs.zh: 每个证明者完成一次证明后，都会由一个验证者读取该证明，其任务是检查证明的正确性。 一个独立的验证者会并排阅读本轮的所有草稿，这使其能够发现共同的盲点，并比较各个证明的优劣。 只有当一份草稿通过两位验证者的检验时，它才会被接受。 两者都具有对抗性：他们一开始就假设每一步都是错误的，除非有理由证明其正确；也假设每个引用都是不准确的，除非经过核实。

paragraphs.en: Each round leaves two artifacts: a record of what was tried, and a ledger of results that have been verified. The record pools attempts by what they were trying to establish, storing with each one the method used and the objection it failed on. The orchestrator and advisor read the record and decide what the next round should do.
paragraphs.zh: 每一轮都会留下两种产物：一份关于尝试过什么内容的记录，以及一份已验证结果的账本。 该记录会根据尝试确立的内容对尝试进行归类，并为每次尝试存储所使用的方法及其失败的原因。 协调员和顾问会读取这份记录，并决定下一轮应该采取什么行动。

paragraphs.en: The ledger accumulates confirmed fragments, such as intermediate lemmas, across rounds. Verifiers often confirm individual lemmas inside proofs they otherwise reject. At the end of a round, an auditor extracts those fragments, rewrites each as a self-contained lemma, and sends it to be verified again in isolation. What survives becomes available to every later prover as something that may be reused without being proved again. The ledger also records dead ends, for example, a bound excluded by a verified counterexample is written down as excluded, so that later rounds do not revisit them.
paragraphs.zh: 账本会在各轮中累积已确认的片段，例如中间引理。 验证者常常会在他们原本拒绝的证明中确认单个引理。 一轮结束时，审计员会提取这些片段，将每个片段改写为自包含的引理，然后单独发送以再次进行验证。 保留下来的内容会成为后续所有证明者可以重复使用而无需重新证明的资源。 账本还会记录死胡同，例如，一个被已验证的反例排除的界限会被标记为“已排除”，以便后续轮次不再重复处理。

paragraphs.en: At the end of each round, a process advisor reviews verification logs, not only from the current round but from the run as a whole, to adjust how subsequent rounds are conducted. It surfaces patterns that become visible over time: repeated mistakes, common gaps in arguments, recurring verification blind spots where one verifier missed but was caught by some other verifier, etc. Based on these observations, it recommends adjustments to the instructions given to provers and verifiers — for example, a warning about a mistake several provers keep making, or a stricter justification standard for the kind of step where earlier drafts cut corners. It also advises the orchestrator on how to allocate prover attempts and how to adjust the instructions given to each prover and verifier for the next round. This is a separate agent because the orchestrator, which must juggle concurrent duties across many agents, rarely has the context window to review and synthesize log trends itself. Note that, neither the advisor nor the orchestrator is permitted a mathematical opinion: they cannot speculate on what the answer is likely to be, recommend a technique, or declare a direction promising or dead.
paragraphs.zh: 每轮结束时，流程顾问都会审查验证日志，不仅包括当前轮次的日志，还包括整个运行过程中的日志，以便调整后续轮次的执行方式。 它会揭示随时间逐渐显现的模式：重复出现的错误、论证中的常见漏洞、反复出现的验证盲点（即某个验证者未能发现但其他验证者成功捕捉到的问题）等。 基于这些观察结果，它会建议对证明器和验证器的指令进行调整——例如，针对多个证明器持续犯错的某类问题发出警告，或对早期草案中简化处理的步骤提出更严格的论证标准。 它还会向协调者提供建议，说明如何分配证明器的尝试次数，以及如何为下一轮调整每个证明器和验证器的指令。 这是一个独立的智能体，因为协调者需要同时处理多个智能体的并行任务，通常没有足够的上下文窗口来亲自审查和总结日志中的趋势。 需要注意的是，顾问和协调者均不被允许持有数学上的观点：他们不能推测答案可能是什么，不能推荐某种技术，也不能宣布某个方向具有前景或已无希望。

sents.en: Based on these observations, it recommends adjustments to the instructions given to provers and verifiers — for example, a warning about a mistake several provers keep making, or a stricter justification standard for the kind of step where earlier drafts cut corners.
sents.zh: 基于这些观察结果，它会建议对证明器和验证器的指令进行调整——例如，针对多个证明器持续犯错的某类问题发出警告，或对早期草案中简化处理的步骤提出更严格的论证标准。

sents.en: It also advises the orchestrator on how to allocate prover attempts and how to adjust the instructions given to each prover and verifier for the next round.
sents.zh: 它还会向协调者提供建议，说明如何分配证明器的尝试次数，以及如何为下一轮调整每个证明器和验证器的指令。

sents.en: This is a separate agent because the orchestrator, which must juggle concurrent duties across many agents, rarely has the context window to review and synthesize log trends itself.
sents.zh: 这是一个独立的智能体，因为协调者需要同时处理多个智能体的并行任务，通常没有足够的上下文窗口来亲自审查和总结日志中的趋势。

sents.en: Note that, neither the advisor nor the orchestrator is permitted a mathematical opinion: they cannot speculate on what the answer is likely to be, recommend a technique, or declare a direction promising or dead.
sents.zh: 需要注意的是，顾问和协调者均不被允许持有数学上的观点：他们不能推测答案可能是什么，不能推荐某种技术，也不能宣布某个方向具有前景或已无希望。

paragraphs.en: When a candidate clears all verification, the orchestrator may continue to explore some remaining promising that may yield a better result, terminating once those avenues are exhausted. Upon termination, a comparator selects the strongest verified proof, a formal writer expands it into a complete manuscript, and a final verification audit checks the compiled document against the accepted proof to ensure no errors were introduced during exposition. The output is a self-contained document that states the theorems and the proofs, with the lemmas it depends on, notation, and background of the problem written out in full, so that it can be read and checked by domain experts who knows nothing about the run that produced it.
paragraphs.zh: 当候选方案通过所有验证后，协调器可能会继续探索一些仍有希望的剩余路径，以期获得更好的结果；一旦这些路径被穷尽，过程便会终止。 终止后，比较器会选择最强的已验证证明，正式撰写者会将其扩展为完整的文稿，最后由最终验证审计对编译后的文档与已接受的证明进行核对，确保在阐述过程中未引入任何错误。 输出是一个自包含的文档，其中陈述了定理及其证明，并完整写明了所依赖的引理、符号以及问题的背景信息，因此即使领域专家对该文档生成时运行的过程一无所知，也能阅读和验证它。

paragraphs.en: The Bulow–Klemperer theorem ( Bulow and Klemperer, 1994 ) establishes that in one-sided auctions, adding a single bidder to a simple mechanism yields at least the revenue of the optimal mechanism for the original market. A natural question is whether a Bulow–Klemperer-type result also holds for two-sided markets. This line of work was initiated by Babaioff et al. (2020a) , who show that, when the buyers’ valuations first-order stochastically dominate the sellers’ costs, adding roughly n ⁡ ( m + 4 ​ m ) n(m+4\sqrt{m}) buyers suffices for a prior-independent mechanism to have gains from trade (GFT) at least that of the first-best GFT, where m m is the number of buyers, n n the number of sellers, and m ≥ n m\geq n . Following up on this, Cai et al. (2024) showed that if one augments both sides of the market then O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) agents suffice. Their analysis, however, requires a large constant, namely at least 20,000 20{,}000 per side. At least two questions remained open, including (i) whether the constant can be improved and (ii) whether it is sufficient to recruit from only one side of the market.
paragraphs.zh: Bulow–Klemperer定理（Bulow和Klemperer，1994）指出，在单边拍卖中，向简单机制添加一名竞拍者，其收益至少能达到原始市场最优机制的收益。一个自然的问题是：Bulow–Klemperer类型的结论是否也适用于双边市场？这一研究方向由Babaioff等人（2020a）开启，他们证明：当买方的估值在一级随机性上支配卖方的成本时，只需添加大约 n ⁡ ( m + 4 ​ m ) n(m+4\sqrt{m}) 名买方，即可使一个先验无关的机制获得至少与第一最佳机制相当的贸易收益（GFT），其中 m m 是买方数量，n n 是卖方数量，且 m ≥ n m\geq n 。在此基础上，Cai等人（2024）进一步证明：如果同时增强市场的双方，则只需 O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) 名智能体即可。然而，他们的分析需要一个较大的常数，即每侧至少需要 20,000 20{,}000。因此，至少有两个问题仍有待解决，包括：（i）该常数是否可以改进；以及（ii）是否只需从市场的一侧招募智能体就足够。

paragraphs.en: In prediction with expert advice, a learner plays a distribution over n n experts, an adversary reveals a loss vector in [ 0 , 1 ] n [0,1]^{n} , and the learner is charged its expected loss relative to the best single expert in hindsight. When the horizon T T is known, multiplicative weights tuned to T T guarantees regret T ​ ln ⁡ n / 2 \sqrt{T\ln n/2} , and the leading constant 1 / 2 1/\sqrt{2} cannot be improved for large n n ( Cesa-Bianchi et al., 1997 ) . An anytime algorithm is given no horizon and must satisfy its bound at every t t simultaneously. The best known anytime guarantee for many experts was t ​ ln ⁡ n \sqrt{t\ln n} , a factor 2 \sqrt{2} worse, and whether that factor was necessary had remained open. For n = 2 n=2 , Luo and Schapire (2014) proved that the anytime regret is strictly larger than the fixed-time regret obtained by Cover (1966) . Later, Harvey et al. (2023) gave the optimal anytime algorithm for n = 2 n=2 but also conjectured that as n → ∞ n\to\infty , the leading constant of the anytime regret and fixed-time regret would coincide. Some evidence towards this conjecture was given by Harvey et al. (2024) , who proved that in continuous time, the anytime and fixed-time constants agree as n → ∞ n\to\infty when the experts follow independent Brownian motions.
paragraphs.zh: 在专家建议预测问题中，学习者对 n 个专家分配一个分布，对抗方揭示一个属于 [0,1]ⁿ 的损失向量，而学习者则根据事后视角下表现最佳的单个专家承担其预期损失。当时间范围 T 已知时，针对 T 调整的乘法权重算法能保证遗憾值为 √(T ln n/2)，且对于较大的 n，领先常数 1/√2 无法进一步改进（Cesa-Bianchi 等人，1997）。任何时刻算法则不提供时间范围，必须同时满足所有 t 时刻的界限。针对多专家问题的最佳已知任何时刻保证为 √(t ln n)，比前述结果差一个因子 √2，而该因子是否为必要值仍是一个未解问题。对于 n=2 的情况，Luo 和 Schapire（2014）证明了任何时刻遗憾值严格大于 Cover（1966）所得到的固定时间遗憾值。随后，Harvey 等人（2023）给出了 n=2 时的最优任何时刻算法，但也推测当 n→∞ 时，任何时刻遗憾值和固定时间遗憾值的领先常数会趋于一致。Harvey 等人（2024）为这一推测提供了一些证据：他们证明了在连续时间中，当专家遵循独立布朗运动时，随着 n→∞，任何时刻和固定时间的常数会一致。

paragraphs.en: With the Cogentic framework, we prove that the leading constant of the fixed-time regret and anytime regret coincide as n → ∞ n\to\infty .
paragraphs.zh: 借助 Cogentic 框架，我们证明了当 n → ∞ 时，固定时间遗憾和任意时刻遗憾的主导常数趋于一致。

paragraphs.en: The proof Cogentic found is elementary. Run one multiplicative-weights instance for each horizon on a geometric grid H m = ( 1 + ε ) m H^{m}=(1+\varepsilon)^{m} and aggregate them with a master multiplicative-weights algorithm. At any time t t some instance is tuned to a horizon in [ t , ( 1 + ε ) ​ t ] [t,(1+\varepsilon)t] and so has regret 1 + ε ​ t ​ ln ⁡ n / 2 \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\sqrt{t\ln n/2} ; it would suffice for the master to track that instance cheaply. The obstruction is that the pool grows with t t while the master’s regret grows with the number of instances it tracks, which would leave a time-dependent overhead in the leading constant. The construction keeps the pool bounded by waking instance m m only at round ⌊ δ ​ H m ⌋ \lfloor\delta H^{m}\rfloor and retiring it after round ⌊ H m ⌋ \lfloor H^{m}\rfloor . Then O ⁡ ( ε − 1 ​ log ⁡ δ − 1 ) O(\varepsilon^{-1}\log\delta^{-1}) instances are awake at once, independent of t t , and at most that many are born during any one instance’s lifetime. This second count matters because when new instances arrive, we must allocate some of the existing probability mass to new instances. Retirement leaves the prefix before ⌊ δ ​ H m ⌋ \lfloor\delta H^{m}\rfloor uncovered, and recursing on it contributes a geometric series 1 + δ + δ + ⋯ 1+\sqrt{\delta}+\delta+\cdots . Taking ε = ln ⁡ ln ⁡ n / ln ⁡ n \varepsilon=\sqrt{\ln\ln n/\ln n} and δ = ε 3 \delta=\varepsilon^{3} makes the grid coarseness, the aggregation overhead, and the recursion together cost a factor 1 + O ⁡ ( ε ) 1+O(\varepsilon) .
paragraphs.zh: Cogentic 找到的证明是初等的。 对每个时间范围，在几何网格 H m = ( 1 + ε ) m H^{m}=(1+\varepsilon)^{m} 上运行一个乘法权重实例，然后用主乘法权重算法将它们汇总。 在任何时刻 t t，某个实例都针对 [ t , ( 1 + ε ) ​ t ] [t,(1+\varepsilon)t] 中的时间范围进行了调整，因此其遗憾值为 1 + ε ​ t ​ ln ⁡ n / 2 \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\sqrt{t\ln n/2}；主算法只需廉价地跟踪该实例即可。 阻碍在于，池子会随着 t t 增长，而主算法的遗憾值则随着其跟踪的实例数量增长，这会在领先常数中留下一个与时间相关的额外开销。 该构造通过仅在回合 ⌊ δ ​ H m ⌋ \lfloor\delta H^{m}\rfloor 唤醒实例 m m，并在回合 ⌊ H m ⌋ \lfloor H^{m}\rfloor 之后将其退役，从而保持池子的有界性。 这样，O ⁡ ( ε − 1 ​ log ⁡ δ − 1 ) O(\varepsilon^{-1}\log\delta^{-1}) 个实例会同时处于活跃状态，与 t t 无关，并且在任何单个实例的生命周期内最多只会诞生这么多实例。 这个第二个计数很重要，因为当新实例到达时，我们必须将部分现有的概率质量分配给这些新实例。 退役操作会使 ⌊ δ ​ H m ⌋ \lfloor\delta H^{m}\rfloor 之前的前缀部分未被覆盖，而对此进行递归则会贡献一个几何级数 1 + δ + δ + ⋯ 1+\sqrt{\delta}+\delta+\cdots。 取 ε = ln ⁡ ln ⁡ n / ln ⁡ n \varepsilon=\sqrt{\ln\ln n/\ln n} 和 δ = ε 3 \delta=\varepsilon^{3}，可使网格的粗糙度、汇总开销以及递归共同产生的成本因子为 1 + O ⁡ ( ε ) 1+O(\varepsilon)。

Let SRev \operatorname{SRev} be the revenue from selling each item separately at a fixed price, and BRev \operatorname{BRev} the revenue from selling the grand bundle at a single price. Let OPT \operatorname{OPT} be the revenue of the optimal mechanism, which may be randomized and arbitrarily complex. Babaioff et al. (2020b) showed that the better of these two simple mechanisms is within a constant factor of optimal: OPT ≤ 6 ⋅ max ⁡ ( SRev , BRev ) \operatorname{OPT}\leq 6\cdot\max(\operatorname{SRev},\operatorname{BRev}) . The duality framework of Cai et al. (2016) later extended this result to a more general setting. For the original single-additive-buyer setting, Ma and Simchi-Levi (2021) improved the factor to 5.2 5.2 . The optimal constant is still unknown, and the best lower bound on the approximation ratio is 2 2 ( Rubinstein, 2016 ) .

paragraphs.en: Automated bidding (autobidding) is now a widely adopted interface for advertisers to bid into high frequency ad auctions. In this interface, advertisers specify high level constraints, such as return-on-spend and budget constraints. To measure efficiency, the literature uses a standard metric known as the price of anarchy (PoA) which is the ratio of the welfare in the optimal allocation and the worst-case equilibrium welfare. Aggarwal et al. (2019) initiated this line of work, showing that the second-price auction (SPA) achieves a tight PoA of 2 2 . Subsequent work by Liaw et al. (2023) proved that no deterministic mechanism—including the first-price auction (FPA)—can beat the PoA barrier of 2 2 in the prior-free setting, even for two bidders. When randomization is combined with non-truthful payments, however, the barrier of 2 2 can be broken for two bidders: Mehta (2022) achieved a two-bidder PoA of approximately 1.89 1.89 via a randomized truthful auction, and Liaw et al. (2023) improved the two-bidder upper bound to 1.8 1.8 using a randomized first-price auction, while proving an n n -bidder lower bound (for even n n ) showing that every anonymous mechanism has PoA ≥ 2 ​ n + 4 n + 4 = 2 − 4 n + 4 \mathrm{PoA}\geq\frac{2n+4}{n+4}=2-\frac{4}{n+4} . At least two questions remain open: (i) what is the exact minimax optimal PoA for n = 2 n=2 bidders, and (ii) for general n ≥ 3 n\geq 3 bidders, whether any mechanism can break the deterministic PoA barrier of 2 2 and match the 2 − Θ ⁡ ( 1 / n ) 2-\Theta(1/n) lower bound.
paragraphs.zh: 自动化竞价（autobidding）现已成为广告商参与高频广告拍卖的广泛采用的接口。 在此接口中，广告商需指定高级别约束条件，例如投入回报率和预算限制。 为衡量效率，相关文献采用了一种标准指标——无政府状态价格（price of anarchy, PoA），即最优分配中的社会福利与最坏均衡社会福利之比。Aggarwal 等人 （2019）开启了这一研究方向，证明了第二价格拍卖（SPA）可实现紧致的 PoA 为 2/2。 Liaw 等人后续的研究 （2023）证明，在没有先验信息的设定下，任何确定性机制——包括第一价格拍卖（FPA）——都无法突破 2/2 的 PoA 屏障，即使只有两名竞价者。 然而，当随机性与非真实支付相结合时，对于两名竞价者而言，2/2 的屏障可以被打破：Mehta（2022）通过随机化真实拍卖实现了两名竞价者的 PoA 约为 1.89；而 Liaw 等人 （2023）则利用随机化第一价格拍卖将两名竞价者的上界改进为 1.8，同时证明了 n 名竞价者（n 为偶数）时的下界为 2(n+4)/(2n+4) = 2 - 4/(n+4)，表明任何匿名机制的 PoA 均 ≥ 2(n+4)/(2n+4)。 至少有两个问题尚未解决：(i) n=2 名竞价者时，精确的最小最大最优 PoA 是多少？以及 (ii) 对于一般的 n≥3 名竞价者，是否存在任何机制能够突破确定性 PoA 的 2/2 屏障，并达到 2 - Θ(1/n) 的下界？

paragraphs.zh: 这样的系统生成候选结果的速度可能快于人们阅读它们的速度，而且随着计算预算的增加，这种差距会越来越大。 一种可能性是使用 Lean（Moura 和 Ullrich，2021）之类的证明助手进行形式化验证，从而通过机械方式确定正确性。 然而，人类对解决方案的理解可能会滞后。 在过去，理解问题的解决方案也常常催生了新的研究方向和问题。 如何平衡这种生成的吞吐量与人类的理解能力，仍然是一个重要的问题。

sents.zh: 这样的系统生成候选结果的速度可能快于人们阅读它们的速度，而且随着计算预算的增加，这种差距会越来越大。

sents.en: One possibility is to formalize in a proof assistant such as Lean ( Moura and Ullrich, 2021 ) , so that correctness is settled mechanically.
sents.zh: 一种可能性是使用 Lean（Moura 和 Ullrich，2021）之类的证明助手进行形式化验证，从而通过机械方式确定正确性。

sents.en: However, human understanding of the solution might lag behind.
sents.zh: 然而，人类对解决方案的理解可能会滞后。

sents.en: In the past, understanding the solution of a problem has also led to new directions and problems being explored.
sents.zh: 在过去，理解问题的解决方案也常常催生了新的研究方向和问题。

sents.en: Balancing out the throughput of this generation and human understanding remains an important question.
sents.zh: 如何平衡这种生成的吞吐量与人类的理解能力，仍然是一个重要的问题。
